props.name: methanol catalyst of difficultly reducible metal oxides with a metallic halide (the invention)
props.description: An oxide of a second-group metal, an oxide of a metal of the third to seventh group as promoter, and a metallic halide.

evidence.quote: We have now discovered that methanol catalysts comprising mixtures of non-reduc- ible or difficultly reducible metallic .oxides may be greatly improved by the addition of a metallic halide.
I. An oxide of a second group (Men- deleeff’s Periodic Table) metal; | JI. An oxide of a metal of the third to geyenth group to serve as a promoter; -
III. A metallic halide.

props.name: halide improves catalyst

evidence.quote: may be greatly improved by the addition of a metallic halide. The precise metal em- ployed in the halide may be either identical with or different from the metal of the oxides.

props.statement: Methanol catalysts comprising mixtures of non-reducible or difficultly reducible metallic oxides are greatly improved by the addition of a metallic halide; the metal of the halide may be identical with or different from the metal of the oxides.

props.name: halide invariably improves

evidence.quote: the pres- ence of a metal halide in the catalyst inva- 116. riably produces greatly improved results,

props.statement: Changes in the proportion of second-group metal to promoter change catalyst effectiveness, but the presence of a metal halide invariably produces greatly improved results.

props.name: halide less than one equivalent

evidence.quote: though the amount of halide added should preferably be less than one chemical equiv- alent of the amount of principal metallic oxide present in the catalyst.

props.statement: The amount of metallic halide need bear no exact weight relation to the other constituents, but should preferably be less than one chemical equivalent of the principal metallic oxide.

props.name: higher yield purer less methane

evidence.quote: yield of methanol than those formerly em- ployed ‘In the art, and at the same time pro- uces avery pure methanol, uncontaminated - by by-products.
that the formation of methane in the proc- ess—with the consequent destruction of val- uable hydrogen—is practically eliminated.

props.statement: The new catalyst gives a higher methanol yield than those formerly employed, a very pure methanol uncontaminated by by-products, and practically eliminates methane formation.

props.name: mixed oxides substitutable

evidence.quote: For example zinc oxide may be replaced by a mixture of 120. zinc oxide and magnesium oxide.

props.statement: A single second-group oxide may be replaced by a mixture of two such oxides (e.g. zinc oxide and magnesium oxide), and a single promoter oxide by a mixture.

props.statement: The substances formed depend, both as to identity and amount, almost entirely on the nature and activity of the catalytic substance; finely divided metals or mixtures of metallic oxides non-reducible under the synthesis conditions cause the production of more or less methanol.

props.name: halide acts as promoter

evidence.quote: The method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not. known to us.
(1) The metallic halide acts as an ordi- nary “promoter” in increasing catalyst activ-

props.note: one of three theories offered; the inventors state the mechanism is not known and forms no part of the invention

props.name: halide forms oxychlorides

evidence.quote: The method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not. known to us.
(2) The metallic halide interacts with other metallic oxides present in the catalyst. to produce oxychloride compounds which, 1n turn, either serve as catalyst promoters,

props.note: one of three theories offered; the inventors state the mechanism is not known and forms no part of the invention
props.statement: The metallic halide interacts with other metallic oxides in the catalyst to produce oxychloride compounds, which serve as promoters or modify the physical state of the mass to give a more active catalyst.

props.name: halide reduced to metal

evidence.quote: The method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not. known to us.

(3) The metallic halide may be reduced by the high pressure contact with hydrogen and carbon oxides during the commence- ment of its use as a catalyst and the resultant finely divided metal may increase the catalyst activity,

props.note: one of three theories offered; the inventors state the mechanism is not known and forms no part of the invention
props.statement: The metallic halide may be reduced by the high-pressure contact with hydrogen and carbon oxides at the start of use, the resulting finely divided metal increasing activity; or it may first react with another metal to give that metal's halide, reduced in the same manner.
